newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rothmans says Australian market uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Rothmans says Australian market uncertain.

text.p: Cigarette manufacturer Rothmans Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday the Australian market was uncertain after price discounting which began in the second half of 1996/97 and led to a decline in second half sales.

Rothmans earlier announced a near doubling in net profit to A$94.73 million for the year ending March 31, which it said was a satisfying result. "The substantial improvement in the consolidated result was primarily due to the recovery by the Australian tobacco operations from the unprecedented price war which occurred during the previous year," the company said.
Rothmans said operating profit before interset, tax and abnormals for Australia at A$93.11 million was A$64.49 million above the previous year.

The company said profits for the second half were lower than the first half mainly due to a lower result for the Australian operations owing to lower cigarette volume and price reductions on specific brands and increased general marketing costs.
Rothmans announced a final dividend of A$1.25, including a special A$1.00 dividend. The company paid a final dividend of 22 cents a year ago.
Rothmans said the special dividend was possible due to the repatriation of the company's retained earnings from New Zealand during the past two years.

"Due to the strength of the company's balance sheet together with the remaining cash reserves, strong cash flow and borrowing capacity, payment of this final divdiend should not inhibit the company's growth potential," the company said.
Total dividend for the year was A$1.50 per share, compared with 42 cents in 1995/96.
Rothmans said it improved cigarette volume and market share in New Zealand where industry cigarette volume rose by three percent in the year.
Profit before interest and tax in New Zealand improved mainly due to improved pricing in the base price cigarette segment, higher cigarette volume and lower production costs.
Rothmans is about 50 percent owned by Rothmans International Ltd which in turn is owned 60 percent by Swiss firm Richemont AG and 40 percent by South African group Rembrandt Group Ltd.
